The run-period blocks C_PL (two-dimensional result; 2.0% on the integrated cross section) and C_PL,5D (sixteen-cell result) include this inconsistency. C_PL,5D has rank 2, is not corrected for the bootstrap noise it contains, and with three groups its size is poorly determined (68% interval on the ratio of its true to its estimated size, 0.73–2.56); it raises the median uncertainty by about 7.8% and that of cell R04 by 14.1%.

proposal: No reported interval has validated coverage. The fake-data tests of Sec. IV H assess bias, not coverage: only event counts fluctuate, with systematic parameters fixed, so interval widths cannot be tested. A coverage test at two of their truths, declared in advance for the covariance without the run-period block, with pseudo-experiments that also draw the flux, interaction and detector uncertainties, stopped at one of its gates before any coverage pseudo-experiment ran: the uncertainties reproduced through its pseudo-experiments disagreed with the covariance blocks they draw, for reasons not established. The two-dimensional covariance has not been independently validated and gives no calibrated significance for generator comparisons; the coverage of its current statistical block and of its total covariance has not been tested, and an earlier statistical band of that result undercovered in its tails in a coverage test at fixed truth. Coverage here is pointwise, for each reported quantity separately; we make no coverage claim on independent simulated samples or simultaneously over all reported bins and projections.
retain: Coverage, how often intervals contain their target over repeated experiments, tests the estimator and the interval construction together.
